newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says Bally's settles suit, buys shrs.
newsitem.headline: Hilton says Bally's settles suit, buys shrs.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp on Friday said Bally's Grand Inc, which is controlled by Hilton, has struck a deal to settle litigation with two investors that includes a stock buyback for $52.75 a share.

Under terms of the settlement, Bally's Grand will acquire 388,561 common shares and 61,285 common stock purchase warrants held by Tower Investment Group Inc and 578,186 common shares shares and 41,413 common stock purcahse warrants held by Executive Life of New York.
The repurchase is set to occure on or before June 26, Hilton said in a statement.
Bally's Grand will pay cash for the stock, and for the warrants it wil pay the difference between $52.75 less the exercise price of warrants, also payable in cash.

Before the settlement, Hilton owned about 85 percent of Bally's Grand shares. Following the deal, it will own about 100 percent. When the court approves the settlement, it will merge Bally's Grand into Hilton or a Hilton unit.
Bally's Grand operates Bally's Las Vegas hotel-casino on the Las Vegas Strip. Hilton acquired its stake in the company when it purchased Bally Entertainment Corp in 1996.

The suit, filed in Delaware Chancery Court last November, alleged that property adjacent to Bally's Las Vegas was sold to Bally Entertainment at less than fair market value and deprived Bally's Grand from a growth opportunity. The defendants, including Hilton and Bally Entertainment, denied the allegations.

In the merger following court approval of the settlement, the 408,862 outstanding Bally's Grand shares not owned by Hilton would be converted into the right to receive $52.75 a share in cash, less attorney's fees, and the 491,784 outstanding warrants not owned by Hilton would be converted into the right to receive the difference between $52.75, less attorney's fees, the exercise price of the warrants in cash.
Bally's Grand said it has received a fairness opinion from investment firm Ladenberg, Thalman & Co regarding the $52.75 per share price.
Bally's Grand shares were up 6-1/4 at 45-1/4 on volume of only 300 shares after the settlement's announcement.
